title: PHI Schema Check evaluator responses
description: Every body the evaluator API returns (evaluator_api.md). Each object is closed. Text fields are the evaluator's own words; nothing from the fact document is echoed except identifiers, paths and locations.

result.description: One practice on one object. object_id is the finding id the fix goal takes. grade is the grade of the evidence the state rests on (E5 when there is none). reason is set for unknown, needs_review and error and null otherwise. how: what to do or how to check, in our words. settled_by is assistant when the assistant's answer settled the line (B28-core): its verdict at E4 on any severity, or a verified location it was asked for at E3; person when the person's option, as relayed, settled it at E4 (with decider_ref, an opaque role or local reference the client chose, never a name, where the rules saw nothing: reason rules_saw_nothing); labelled by assurance either way; Custosa's own grade rules hold for unlabelled lines only. assistant is the assistant's verdict and its reason, graded E4, on any line it answered, so the person sees it under an item that stays open.

decider_ref.description: Contract 2.5: an opaque reference to who decided, chosen by the client: a role or local reference, never a name or email. On a line a person's option settled where Custosa's rules saw nothing (reason rules_saw_nothing). Custosa can't check it: it is the accountability, not a proof.

assistant.description: The assistant's verdict on this line's practice, graded E4. reason is Custosa's words for the reason_code it sent (enums.REASON_WORDS), or for a remembered verdict that it is remembered; never the assistant's own text: shown, never observed. It settles the line only where Custosa's facts don't contradict it, labelled assistant_decided, and never counts in the verified percent.

assurance.description: Who stands behind the result (B28-core): absent means custosa, Custosa's own reading. assistant_decided: the assistant's verdict at E4; assistant_decided_located: a location it named, confirmed by the inspector, at E3; person_decided (person_decided_committed for one replayed from the project's record): the person's option, as relayed by the assistant, at E4; open: an answer or decision moved the result and it stays open. custosa_on_cited_facts (contract 2.6, T29 line item h): a pass Custosa judged by its own rules on facts the assistant cited (fact document cited_facts), at E3, shown as "Custosa judged on facts the AI cited". Only custosa counts in the verified percent.

facts_needed.description: Contract 2.6 (T29 line item h): on an authz-every-handler, write-fields-allowlisted or rls-policies-scoped line, the candidates the inspector listed whose deciding facts are still missing, each with those fields (enums.FACT_FIELDS); the next step asks for them. It names a field and its values, never the values that pass. Absent when nothing is needed.

committed.description: Contract 2.3 (T23 B50): what each committed entry on this object came to, sorted by kind (decision, suppression, grant), then by key: at most one decision, one suppression and three grants. Present only when an entry matched the result (any outcome but seal_mismatch, no_match and other_account). It never changes state, reason or grade until B28; an accepted fail stays a fail.

observed_problem.description: Custosa observed a problem here (a role or command it saw): an evidence hold that only a fail or leaving it open settles. Present only when true.

decision.description: The structured decision this run offers the person on an open line (B28-core, design v3 section 2.1.4): the question, why it is asked, what Custosa read, and the options with the state each settles as (null leaves the item open). An option sent back as decisions {object_id, option} settles the line only when this run offers it.

saw.description: Contract 2.5 (docs/empty-match-settle.md v2): on a line whose rules saw nothing of the object, counts only, because it rides on every such line. matched: nothing (the rules ran and matched no item or violation of the object, or a scanner found nothing) or not_run (they never ran here); stack_count: the practice's rule stacks whose language this run read (a stack's rule file is practice.stack); files_covered: the files the inspector analysed (null when unknown). What Custosa read and what to look for are in the practice's guidance, get_result part guidance (saw, look_for). A pass or not_applicable here settles only as a person's option sent with decider_ref.

evidence.description: What a result rests on: a rule id (rule, secret), a query id (catalog), a setting name (platform), a question id (answer) or a collector (collector), with the location where there is one.

question.description: A judgement the rules can't make. Answered in the next call's answers field with this question_id and object_id. practice_id: the practice that asks it, whose guidance get_result part guidance returns (B52). expects: the construct kind a location answer must point at for E3 (null when no location is asked). why, look_for and settles (optional, T18): the reason the item is open, where to look and what each allowed answer does, from the practice's own text.

why.description: The reason code the item is open on (result.reason).

look_for.description: Where to look: the files, constructs or settings that settle it.

settles.description: What each allowed answer does to the result, one line per answer.

brief.description: T18: one question for every listed object of one practice, asked once. Each object is answered as its own question in the next call's answers field, with this question_id and the object's object_id; intake, grading and E3 checks are those of a question. An object in a brief is not repeated in questions, and still counts as open until it is answered.

why.description: The reason code the item is open on (result.reason).

look_for.description: Where to look: the files, constructs or settings that settle it.

settles.description: What each allowed answer does to the result, one line per answer.

fix.description: A fix for one finding, in our words and code: steps to follow, the migration SQL where there is one, the files it touches, how to undo it and how the next check confirms it.

readiness.description: Contract A (T29 r1): readiness counts practices, not objects. A practice's state is the worst of its results: fail, then open (needs_review, unknown or error), then pass, then not_applicable; a practice whose registry applies_to matches the app with no reading is unread, never pass, and one whose applies_to doesn't match is out of the practice counts, the score and ready (unless any of its results is other than a pass or not_applicable, or is a hold; a practice is out only on a positive read of another platform or stack by the inspector's own collectors (an empty, unrecognised or assistant-written read takes nothing out)); counts and by_severity still count every result, as the findings lines list them. ready only with at least one pass practice, every practice pass or not_applicable (no fail, no open item at any severity, no unread practice) and no unresolved assistant concern; a confirmed open concern makes the practice it names open, or counts as one more open line. percent is verified by Custosa (E1 or E2); score counts every pass practice and always travels with score_label; pass_by_grade and breakdown say who decided; practice_counts counts the practices by state and severity, and by_practice gives each practice's line. A person's decision recorded without an option is shown, never counted. Production readiness (ready with environment production) needs environment value production from source setup; from source answer the state is not_ready in production.

verified_state.description: The badge's word (T27 C69, contract A), which the public badge and page show: the same rule as state, with a pass or not_applicable practice counted only at the grades custosa (E1, E2) and custosa_on_cited_facts (E3). A practice the assistant or a person settled (pass or not_applicable) never makes it ready. Inside the session state stands.

percent.description: percent_verified: practices whose pass rests only on Custosa's own reading (E1 or E2) over every practice line but a not_applicable one Custosa read itself, plus one line per confirmed open concern that names no practice line; half up, never 100 while one isn't such a pass, null when nothing applies.

counts.description: Results by shown state; a pass or not_applicable Custosa judged on facts the assistant cited (E3), or the assistant or a person settled, is counted in custosa_on_cited_facts, assistant_decided or person_decided, never in pass or not_applicable. A labelled fail stays in fail.

critical.description: critical results by state, and concern_open: the assistant's open confirmed concerns at critical (B51). concern_open counts concerns, the other keys results: never sum them.

high.description: high results by state, and concern_open: the assistant's open confirmed concerns at high (B51). concern_open counts concerns, the other keys results: never sum them.

medium.description: medium results by state, and concern_open: the assistant's open confirmed concerns at medium (B51). concern_open counts concerns, the other keys results: never sum them.

low.description: low results by state, and concern_open: the assistant's open confirmed concerns at low (B51). concern_open counts concerns, the other keys results: never sum them.

applicable.description: Practices in the area but a not_applicable one Custosa read itself: verified_pass's denominator.

verified_pass.description: Practices in the area whose pass rests only on E1 or E2.

settled_pass.description: Pass practices in the area, of any grade.

score_applicable.description: Practices in the area but any not_applicable: settled_pass's denominator.

pass_by_grade.description: Pass practices by the grade they rest on, so the E3 count (custosa_on_cited_facts) and the settled counts show beside percent and score. They sum to the pass practices.

concern_lines.description: Confirmed open concerns that name no practice: one more open line each, in the score's and the percent's denominators. The percent's denominator is the sum of by_area's applicable plus this; the score's, the sum of by_area's score_applicable plus this.

practice_counts.description: Every practice counted by its state and severity (contract A): fail, open, unread, pass and not_applicable, complete on every response; by_practice gives the lines.

by_practice.description: One line per practice counted (contract A), sorted by practice id: its state, the weakest grade its pass or not_applicable rests on (null for fail, open and unread) and its severity. Practice numbers, never compared with the index's result_counts.

score.description: The score: pass practices of any grade over every practice line but a not_applicable one, plus one line per confirmed open concern that names no practice line (a fixed concern is neutral, a dismissed or unconfirmed one out). Never shown without score_label.

score_label.description: "N% settled, M% verified by Custosa", or why there is no score.

blockers.description: What keeps the state not_ready, by severity, the same counts the headline and the public badge name (app.readiness.blocker_phrases). Each result counts in one kind at most (B28-core second review): hold is a result whose F4 class is hold (app.core.assurance.f4_class: observed_problem or definer_hold set, an evidence-hold reason such as collection_truncated, answer_contradicted, code_not_verified, location_not_confirmed, table_not_resolved, definer_function_unjudged, exposure_suspected, helper_not_reached_from_handlers, unclassified_table_exposed, non_runtime_file or fact_missing, or a reason in no class); person_only is a result whose F4 class is person_only for assistant_contested; a result person_only for rules_saw_nothing alone counts by its state, as below. Every other result counts by its shown state, at every severity (contract A): fail, needs_review, unknown, error. A run problem (evaluator_error, preflight_failed) counts as error or unknown by its state. unread counts practices, not results: a practice that applies with no reading. Unresolved assistant concerns and production named by the assistant also keep it not_ready and are not counted here.

breakdown.description: Who stands behind the settled results (design v3 section 2.1.5 part 2), always next to the state.

verified_by_custosa.description: Settled pass and not_applicable results Custosa observed.

assistant_decided.description: Settled pass and not_applicable results the assistant decided; located: those on a confirmed location.

person_decided.description: Settled pass and not_applicable results a person decided, as relayed; committed: from the committed state file.

concerns.description: The assistant's concerns by where they stand.

closed_by_assistant.description: Fixed or dismissed concerns resting on the assistant's word alone (review N6): counted in rests_on_assistant at critical and high, and in rests_on_assistant_any.

rests_on_assistant.description: True when a critical or high pass or not_applicable was decided by the assistant or a person, or a critical or high concern was fixed or dismissed by the assistant.

rests_on_assistant_any.description: True when any pass or not_applicable was decided by the assistant or a person, or the assistant marked a concern fixed or dismissed it.

collection_summary.description: What the evaluation stood on, from the fact document after fact building: every collector and query, with a missing one shown as failed, and the status of supabase.edge_functions as read (worst of with the files collector).

edge_functions.description: supabase.edge_functions' status and reason after fact building (evaluator_api.md section 1.7): the worse of its own and the files collector's, and not_run (no config.toml) only after a complete walk.

report.description: On the ending response (status done): what the person reads. trust_note says the evaluator never saw the code and that the grade beside each result says how it was known. hashed_names_note is the one line explaining hashed names (u_ and 16 hex), present whenever any result names one, null otherwise. needs_review is the one end-of-run list for the person: one line per underlying item (an object, or a project line per reason for results naming no object) with what to look at. Since T29 o1b 3d-1 the response carries the fixed lines; decisions and concerns are the index's list selectors (report.decisions, report.concerns.<status>), and by_state and needs_review are the index's result_counts and open groups (T29-P1-C89 point 2).

by_state.description: The object ids of every result, by state, sorted. Since T29 o1b 3d-1 never on the response: the index's result_counts and its practice, fail and open lines say the same, and get_result with a state selector lists them. A pass or not_applicable Custosa judged on cited facts, or the assistant or the person settled, is listed under custosa_on_cited_facts, assistant_decided or person_decided instead, as readiness counts it.

decider_ref.description: Contract 2.5: an opaque reference to who decided, chosen by the client: a role or local reference, never a name or email. On a line a person's option settled where Custosa's rules saw nothing (reason rules_saw_nothing). Custosa can't check it: it is the accountability, not a proof.

decisions.description: Every decision on record for this session, recorded and shown, never a pass. source person_confirmation: a person_confirmation answer the assistant relayed (confirmed, not_confirmed, declined); source decisions: an entry of the evaluate body's decisions block, accepted only with decided_by person (accepted, declined, not_applicable). An entry with an option (B28-core) is the person's option on a line's decision, as relayed by the assistant: outcome accepted when it settled the line (person_decided), refused when the line didn't offer it this run, recorded otherwise.

enum: Names shown as u_ and 16 hex characters couldn't be sent as written, so the inspector hashed them on your machine; only your machine can map them back.

dependency_folders_note.description: The one line saying exempt dependency and build-output folders were listed but not read, present whenever the fact document listed one, null otherwise.
enum: Dependency and build-output folders (such as node_modules, or an ignored dist) were listed but not read; results speak for the app's own code only.

needs_review.description: The end-of-run list, grouped by cause (B9): one line per cause an item is open for, so the person makes one decision per cause, not one per object. Every needs_review result is on the line of its reason; every open result whose database catalog wasn't read (no database connected, or an engine the inspector can't read such as SQLite or MySQL) is on one line of its own, reason collector_not_run, whatever its state. A line names the objects its results rest on (each once per cause), every practice, the object ids of those results, the cause's reason and what to look at. A cause too long for one line continues on the next line, and a result whose objects don't fit one line is named on each line they continue on. A person's answer is recorded as a decision, never a pass.

look.description: What to look at for this item, in our words.

state.description: Contract 2.3 (T23 B50): the committed block, as replayed. Present when the body carried committed. sent, by_outcome and to_commit_total are on the response; unmatched (by index into the sent list, never the entry), to_commit and not_committed are kept in the call's store and named in the index's lists (get_result select list state.<name>). to_commit is empty until B28 brings a person's options.

concerns.description: B51: every assistant concern's id by where it stands, in the order raised. Since T29 o1b 3d-1 kept in the call's store and named in the index's lists (get_result select list report.concerns.<status>), not on the response.

committed_state.description: Contract 2.3 (T23 B50): the committed block's replay, closed. Shown as report.state on the ending response and as the top-level state on every response. Since T29 o1b 3d-1 the response carries the fixed lines; the lists (unmatched, to_commit, not_committed) are the index's list selectors (state.<list>).

to_commit.description: Entries the CLI writes to the state file (contract 2.3 §5.2): only for this body's person choices the core accepted whose token still equals the one the person was asked on. Empty until B28 brings options.

to_commit_total.description: Every to_commit entry of this response: the list itself is kept in the call's store (get_result select list state.to_commit), so the CLI can say how many entries the assistant hasn't fetched.

evaluate_response.description: 200 from POST /v1/evaluate for an evaluation goal (check, fix, verify) (fact_document sent). One body, never paged (T29 o1b): the fixed envelope, the report's and the state's fixed lines, this call's own parts (delta on a verify, concern_outcomes, not_used) and index, which counts every result and names every fail, open group, question, concern, fix and list with its get_result selector. The results themselves, their guidance, fixes, proofs and references are kept in the call's store and returned by get_result. The same digest, ruleset_id and arguments give byte-identical results.

evaluator_version.description: RC2: the evaluator build that answered (Cloud Run's revision, else the image's build label). Set on every evaluation response and get_result answer, never on an advice response.

inspector_version.description: RC2: the fact document's inspector_version, echoed (the same pattern).

state.description: Contract 2.3 (T23 B50, P1 C75 ruling 1): the committed state's fixed lines on every response, while questions are still open too. Present when the body carried committed. On the ending response it mirrors report.state. Its lists (to_commit, not_committed, unmatched) are kept in the call's store and named in the index's lists.

learning.description: Whether this account's learning is on now (its setting, its kind and its company; T27-P1-C121). Send a verdict's or concern's note only after an answer said on; while off, or when an answer doesn't say, a verdict goes without its note and a concern with note_kept_local. A fetch repeats the value its evaluation gave.

report_url.description: T27 D10 (T27-P1-C84 item 2): on a done check only, the account page where this run's result is listed, so the assistant can say where the score is on the website.

contract_version.description: The request and response contract the evaluator speaks (contract 2.2, T23 B49; 2.4 since B51); absent from an older evaluator.

guidance.description: B52 (T23-P1-C104, C109): not sent since T29 o1b 3d-1. A practice's guidance is kept once in the call's store and returned by get_result part guidance. Kept here so an older body still validates.

concerns.description: B51 (contract 2.4, review N1): the assistant's concerns for this project, since T29 o1b 3d-1 kept in the call's store and named by the index (index.concerns, or index.concerns_grouped past the client limit), never on the response: every concern, those raised this call first, then those decided this call, then the unresolved, then the closed, newest first in each. report.concerns indexes every id by status and readiness.breakdown.concerns counts them.

concern_outcomes.description: B51: absent when this call sent no concern_decisions: each decision's outcome, in the order sent.

not_used.description: T27 S3-1: absent when every answer this call sent was for a question this session issued. Each answer that was not, in the order sent, at most 20: it was not applied to any result, not charged and not part of the digest, and the rest of the call was answered as if it had not been sent. reason not_issued: no question of this session asked that object_id and question_id. reason location_too_wide (owner D8): its location, or one of its at spans, covers 30 lines or more; only that answer is set aside, and it never counts as a pass.

concerns_saved.description: B51: present, false, when this call's concern changes were not all kept: the write failed (send the call's concerns and concern_decisions again) or some decisions were refused because another call changed those concerns meanwhile (concern_outcomes reason changed_meanwhile: read them as listed, then decide again). Absent when they were kept.

advice_response.description: 200 from POST /v1/evaluate for an advice goal (plan, pattern, explain; no facts read), or a fetch of one. content is the advice as JSON text of one object: plan {summary, entities, split, access_model, audit_and_retention, keep_out_of_logs_and_ai, migration, practices, doubts?, doubt_categories?}; pattern {pattern} or {pattern: null, need, stack, note, practices}; explain {practice} with the practice's user-facing fields only (id, area, title, property, applies_to, severity, severity_rationale, severity_raise?, mechanisms, guidance, limits?, sources, review_by); or {error, ...} naming what the evaluator knows instead. content is whole when the answer fits the client's tool-output limit; nothing pages. Past it, content holds the advice's smallest top-level parts whole and advice_index names every other part, each returned by get_result (T29 o1b).

contract_version.description: The request and response contract the evaluator speaks (contract 2.2, T23 B49; 2.4 since B51); absent from an older evaluator.

advice_index.description: T29 (o): present only when the whole advice would pass the client's tool-output limit. One line per top-level part not in content: its key, its number of entries, its size in characters, and the get_result select that returns it (whole, or a sub_index of its entries). content plus every part listed is the whole advice.

error_response.description: Any refusal or failure. Never charged. at: the JSON pointer of the first refused field of the fact document (keys and indexes only, never a value;  for the whole body). current_ruleset_id: with update_inspector. balance, currency, top_up_url: with insufficient_balance. retry_after_seconds: with rate_limited, balance_reserved and unavailable.

contract_version.description: The request and response contract the evaluator speaks (contract 2.2, T23 B49; 2.4 since B51); absent from an older evaluator.

device_token_response.description: 200 from POST /v1/device/poll once the person has approved.

device_error_response.description: 400 from POST /v1/device/poll while not approved (RFC 8628 section 3.5). interval: with slow_down.

guidance.description: B52 (design v3 2.1.1): one practice's guidance (practice_id) for the assistant, explanation only. It never changes a state, grade, reason or option. why: why the practice matters; look_for: places and forms to look at, as {stack, items} for any and each stack this run saw (every stack when the files weren't read in full); examples: one safe and one unsafe shape; saw: what Custosa saw on this run, worded as scope, never as absence; answer_with: the codes the practice accepts.

concern.description: B51 (contract 2.4): one assistant concern, by its server id. Its closed metadata (category, area and file_kind absent only on a stored entry this core can't read, listed unconfirmed at critical with no options), where it stands (status, and in next.awaiting the step it waits on: confirm, dismiss_reason, severity or fix; null once closed), its label in the person's words and the ids of the options for its next step, whose labels are in the response's concern_options. A concern's text is never sent back (review N8): the assistant keeps its own copy. A fix is the assistant's or a person's word, never verified by Custosa.

by.description: Present on an option only a person may choose here: send it with decided_by person only after the person chose it.

outcome.description: This call's decisions on this concern: refused when any of them was refused (not an option for its decider where the concern stood, or the concern changed meanwhile; the concern unchanged by it), else accepted. Each decision's own outcome and reason are in the response's concern_outcomes.

concern_options.description: B51 (review N2): the labels, in the person's words, of every option id the concerns the index lists offer; absent when none offers one (only closed or unreadable concerns).

concern_outcome.description: B51: what became of one concern decision this call sent, in the order sent. accepted: applied (or not_sure, which moves nothing). already_applied: the last call that changed the concern applied this same decision by the same decider (a retry): nothing changes. refused, the concern unchanged by it, with its reason: not_an_option (not an option for its decider where the concern stood), unknown_concern (an id outside the project's ledger: never raised, expired or pruned) or changed_meanwhile (another call changed the concern after this one read it: read it as listed and send the decision again).

delta.description: T29 item 1: a verify only, within 4,000 characters. The findings (results shown in state fail, needs_review, unknown or error) of the last check or verify of the same project root (against names its goal; null when none is kept, and then nothing is compared) against this verify: cleared, now pass or not_applicable on Custosa's own reading or on a verdict labelled settled by the AI (by_ai counts those; T29-P1-C6); still_open, now in any other state or no longer in the results (unread counts those now unknown or error, or gone: a finding whose fact went missing is never cleared), naming only those now failing and the unread ones, the rest counted; a result a person's decision settled stays here, counted as person_decided; new, a finding now that was none in the last run. fails counts the fails in each list (in the last run for cleared, now for the others). Each list puts fails first, then by object id; past the budget, object ids are cut from the end of the longest list and cut is true. count is always exact.

result_index.description: T29 (o), contract C: the whole result of this call, never cut. result_counts count every result; one line per practice (worst wins: fail, then open, then pass, then not_applicable); every fail on one line, or, when those lines alone would pass the client's tool-output limit, the fails grouped by practice with fails_grouped; the open results grouped by practice; every question in full; one line per concern and per fix; and the named lists. Each group names the get_result selector that lists it.

questions_grouped.description: T29-P1-C95 (B): present when the questions in full would pass the client's tool-output limit (questions is then empty): one line per practice and question kind, with its count and the {"list": "questions.<practice>"} select that returns every question that practice asks.

concerns_grouped.description: o1b 3d-1: present when fails, questions and concerns in full would pass the client's tool-output limit (concerns is then empty): one line per concern status with its count and the {"list": "concerns.<status>"} select.

get_result_response.description: T29 (o): a get_result answer. matched is the full count; results hold every match with the part asked for, or, when they would pass the client's tool-output limit, sub_index holds one line per match with its own selector. A single match is always whole. A selector that matches nothing answers matched 0 with the values that would match (values). is_fetch_only, charged 0.

anyOf.description: One match with the part asked for (null when this result has none).

proof_id.description: T29-P1-C99: the id verify's proof_results names this proof by.

oneOf.description: The practice's dated sources and review date, with the registry entries of the vendors this result's evidence names (vendors_unlisted: named, with no entry).

items.description: A dated BAA registry entry (T29 (l)): reference knowledge, never evidence that this app signed one.

anyOf.description: One part or entry of the last advice answer (advice goals): its key (key or key#i), the member name when the part is an object, and its content as JSON text.

note.description: T29-P1-C95 (A): on part proof of a check or verify, which builds no fixes: says that a fix call builds the proofs.

result_selector.description: A get_result selector (request.schema.json get_result): exactly one of these.
